subject: Post-call: model evals & multilingual checks - EU/APAC next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrova <elena@globex-retail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: model evals & multilingual checks - EU/APAC next steps

Hi Elena

Thanks again for the productive discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + intent classification across EU (DE/FR/PL/ES/IT) and APAC (JP/KR/EN-AU) locales.
- Key quality concerns: locale-specific date/currency formatting, entity extraction for local product SKUs, and hallucination on regional intents.

Recommended evaluation scope (what we'll run):
- Models to benchmark: Llama-2-Chat-70B (8-bit quantized), Mistral-Instruct-7B, Redwood-13B (quantized profile).
- Metrics: multilingual NLU accuracy, intent F1, ROUGE-L for summarization, and hallucination rate (manual spot-check + model-based detector).
- Prompt/seed sets: please share your representative prompt sets and any locale-specific test cases (date formats, address formats, sample tickets).

Immediate asks for Globex:
1) Share prompt_sets.csv (a few hundred rows with examples per locale).
2) Any annotated labels or current model outputs for reference.
3) Confirm whether PII redaction should be applied before evaluation or if we should evaluate on masked originals.

What Redwood will deliver:
- Initial eval matrix comparing the three recommended models across EU and APAC locales (10 business days after we receive prompt sets).
- A short benchmark PDF with per-locale callouts + recommended config (tokenization/temperature/batching) and a quality regression checklist.
- Follow-up call to review results and discuss tradeoffs (cost vs latency vs quality).

Links: I uploaded our recommended evaluation template and past benchmark examples to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-globex-eval
HubSpot deal id: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765

CC'ing Neha (ML lead) and Vivek (solutions) to pick this up on our side.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

---
Attachments: eval-plan.md (evaluation checklist & timeline stub)

From: Elena Petrova <elena@globex-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@globex-retail.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call: model evals & multilingual checks - EU/APAC next steps

Hi Marissa

Thanks for the clear note and next steps. We're aligned on scope. I've attached our current prompt_sets_v1 and a small sample of labeled tickets per locale. Quick notes:
- EU: we have heavier volume in DE/FR/ES; also a small but important Polish chunk (we'll add more examples next week).
- APAC: JP/KR are high priority for sentiment/intent; EN-AU is smaller but needs region-specific spelling variants.
- On PII: we prefer redacted data for external vendors; I'll send a redacted CSV and a raw/secured version for your team under our S3 share (we'll add access for redwood@redwood.com).

Attaching: globex_prompt_sets_v1.csv, benchmarks_eu_apac_v2.pdf

Can you confirm whether Redwood will run tokenization checks (subword break issues) as part of the evaluation? Also, can you include locale-aware date parsing as a metric? We've seen models normalize dates to US format which breaks downstream flows.

Thanks

Elena Petrova
Head of ML Ops | Globex Retail
elena@globex-retail.com

---
Attachments: globex_prompt_sets_v1.csv, benchmarks_eu_apac_v2.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrova <elena@globex-retail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: model evals & multilingual checks - EU/APAC next steps

Elena

Appreciate the fast turnaround and for sharing both redacted + raw paths. To confirm: yes, we'll include tokenization diagnostics and a locale-aware date normalization check in the evaluation matrix. Specific plan: 

1) Ingest redacted CSV first and run baseline evals for all three recommended models.
2) Run tokenizer/subword breakdown report per locale (OOV rate, avg tokens per example).
3) Run locale-aware date/currency normalization tests and produce failure examples.
4) Produce a hallucination spot-check (10 examples per locale) and flag any high-risk failure modes.

Timeline: we'll start as soon as we have S3 access (or you can upload to the Drive link). Expect deliverable in ~10 business days. If you need a faster turnaround for a limited-scope pilot (e.g., DE/JP only), we can prioritize that in 3-4 business days.

Neha/Vivek
can you confirm resource allocation and whether we should use Redwood-13B for lower latency/price baseline and Llama-2-Chat-70B as our high-quality reference? Also note we should test quantized configs to ensure performance parity for long summaries.

Thanks,
Marissa

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Petrova <elena@globex-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: model evals & multilingual checks - EU/APAC next steps

Marissa / team

Ack. I'll lead the evaluation and here's the proposed execution plan (high level):
- Data ingest: validate redaction, sample distribution per-locale, and mapping of labels.
- Tokenization checks: compute OOV/tokenization mismatches using our tokenizer suite for each model.
- Metrics: intent F1, NER token F1 (where labels exist), ROUGE-L for summaries, and a hallucination flag per-example.
- Thresholds: will set early-warning thresholds (e.g., >5% hallucination or >10pt drop in F1 vs. English baseline) to call out regressions.
- Security: we will run everything in our Private eval environment (no external network) until Globex approves raw data usage.

Questions for Globex:
1) Confirm the list of locales to prioritize (DE/FR/ES/PL/IT / JP/KR / EN-AU).
2) Any performance SLOs (latency/99th) we should target in the report? That affects model/config suggestions.
3) For redaction: what token should we use for PII placeholders (e.g., <REDACTED>)? It affects token counts.

I'll upload the eval-plan.md with the checklist and exact scripts to the shared folder by EOD.

Neha Kapoor
ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

---
Attachments: eval-plan.md

From: Elena Petrova <elena@globex-retail.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 10:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call: model evals & multilingual checks - EU/APAC next steps

Thanks team

All good. Confirming locales: DE/FR/ES/PL/IT + JP/KR + EN-AU.
PII placeholder: please use <REDACTED>.
Performance SLO: target p99 latency under 800ms for short responses (<128 tokens) for the baseline Redwood-13B config; we'll accept higher latency for the 70B reference but want the tradeoff documented.

I'll add a quick pilot request: can you prioritize DE and JP for the 3-4 business day quick-turn pilot? We want to show the engineering leads early wins.

Please schedule a 30-minute review for results week-of Mar 2
any day Tue/Wed after 10am CET works for us.

Elena
